title: MyPEEPS Mobile LITE: Limited Interaction Efficacy Trial of MyPEEPS Mobile to Reduce HIV Incidence and Better Understand the Epidemiology of HIV among Young Men
text: Addressing the End the HIV Epidemic initiatives, this study will use innovative electronic methods (e.g., social media with community informed advertisements) to recruit and retain a large national sample young men to better understand correlates of HIV incidence within the context of a theoretically-grounded social- ecological framework. In addition to the epidemiologic aim of the proposed research, we will test the efficacy of MyPEEPS Mobile, a promising mHealth HIV prevention intervention in reducing HIV incidence among young men.

title: Investigating the role of Cdkn2a in lung adenocarcinoma metastasis
text:
Metastasis causes most lung cancer deaths, but it is poorly understood due to difficulties in
modeling the complexities of metastasis in a relevant, high-throughput and quantitative manner.
This project will employ innovative genetically engineered mouse models to understand how
Cdkn2a and its genetic interactions regulate metastatic ability, which could reveal therapeutic
targets for metastatic lung cancer.

title: AAV-mediated PERM1 Overexpression as a New Therapy for Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction
text:
Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (known as HFrEF) affects millions of Americans, yet effective
therapies remain lacking. HFrEF is marked by contractility dysfunction and mitochondrial impairment, with
no current therapies targeting both cardiac contractility and mitochondrial function. This project proposes
a novel therapeutic strategy to simultaneously restore muscle function and energy metabolism in HFrEF
through therapeutic gene delivery of PERM1, a muscle-specific mitochondrial regulator, aiming to better
treat this lethal disease.

title: Epigenetic drivers of stem cell fitness in aging hematopoiesis
text:
Chronic, low-grade inflammation is a hallmark of aging and leads to the expansion of mutant hematopoietic stem
cell clones, but the molecular mechanisms behind this process remain elusive. This proposal aims to
mechanistically dissect how DNA methylation drives TET2-mutant stem cell fitness when exposed to age-related
chronic inflammation. This research is relevant to public health because it will inform the development of
therapeutic strategies to halt somatic clonal expansions, prevent their deleterious functional consequences and
ultimately improve healthspan.

title: Multimodal Analysis of Gestational Health and Placental Injury in Opioid-Affected Pregnancies
text:
Our proposal centers on the adverse impact of illicit opioid use during pregnancy and its devastating
consequences on the mother, fetus, and the placenta. By integrating multimodal technologies and
assessments, including single-cell RNA transcriptomics, spatial transcriptomics and chip-cytometric methods,
and analysis of placental extracellular vesicle, we will shed new light on mechanisms underlying opioid-
dependent placental dysfunction and diseases during pregnancy and infancy.

title: Modeling and Removing Visual Impairments for Endoscopic Kidney Stone Surgery
text:
Each year, over 100,000 patients require an endoscopic (i.e. minimally invasive) surgery for kidney stone disease
in the United States and approximately 25% require a repeat surgery. Visual impairments from debris and fluid
during operation can result in increased difficulty tracking kidney stones during the operation. This study aims to
create computer vision and machine learning models which quantify and remove the visual impairments
encountered to improve endoscopic treatment of kidney stones.

title: Synaptic defects caused by mitochondrial complex I dysfunction
text:
Health Relevance Narrative: Loss of mitochondrial function can be debilitating in the nervous system, as
evident from its association with numerous neurological diseases and disorders – including forms of
Parkinson’s Disease, Leigh Syndrome, or other movement disorders. In order to develop more effective
treatments for mitopathies of the nervous system, we need better understanding of the cellular and synaptic
consequences of mitochondrial dysfunction. This proposal addresses that problem, using a genetic model of
Mitochondrial Complex I dysfunction.

title: Targeting FAK-NEDD9 protein-protein interaction to prevent focal adhesion assembly and vascular proliferation in pulmonary arterial hypertension
text:
Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a disease characterized by abnormal changes to the structure of lung
arteries (i.e., ‘remodeling’), and is a major cause of heart failure and death among patients with various disorders
of the heart, lung, blood, and connective tissue organ systems. Despite its importance to outcome in patients
with PAH, effective therapies that reverse or prevent lung blood vessel remodeling are lacking. We propose an
innovative approach that targets the key remodeling protein, NEDD9, selectively using a novel small molecule
to establish a potential new treatment for PAH patients.

title: Myelin Content and Cognitive Trajectories in Young Adults Living with Virally Suppressed HIV
text:
Individuals living with HIV continue to experience cognitive symptoms that impact daily function despite
treatment with antiretroviral therapy and research thus far has heavily focused on cognitive impairment rather
than earlier time points prior to the development of impairment. Additionally, our findings show that decreased
myelin, a key component of white matter in brain, may be injured in individuals living with HIV at risk for
developing cognitive impairment. We will focus on a unique cohort of young adults, ages 18 to 34 years, living
with HIV and evaluate the pathology underlying brain injury in this cohort using a new imaging sequence that
focuses on myelin content, blood markers of inflammation, and standardized cognitive assessments over time
to better understand the cognitive trajectory and risk factors for suboptimal cognitive performance in young
adults living with HIV.

title: Genetic Underpinnings of CM and SM and Effect on Brain Development
text: Chiari type I malformation (CM1), the herniation of the cerebellum through the foramen magnum into the spinal canal, is one of the most common pediatric neurological conditions, found in approximately 1 in 1000 individuals. CM1 is characterized by the herniation of the cerebellum through the foramen magnum into the spinal canal, often leading to syringomyelia (SM), a fluid-filled cyst within the spinal canal, obstruction of normal cerebrospinal fluid flow, compression of the brainstem and numerous neurological symptoms. We now have identified some of the first genetic causes of CM1 and have identified idiopathic macrocephaly as a major etiological subtype of CM1. By identifying additional genetic factors underlying CM1 and CM1-related imaging biomarkers, we hope to uncover additional CM1 subtypes and their genetic basis. Additionally, our goal is to understand the role of CM1- associated genetic variation that we have already identified by modeling specific genetic variants in zebrafish to determine what systems are affected (brain, spine, skull, ventricular system) that lead to the common outcome of hindbrain displacement. Earlier and more accurate diagnoses for CM1 patients will have profound effects, informing clinical decisions regarding who should undergo surgery (versus CSF shunting vs surgery+spinal fusion vs observation, etc) and along what time frame.

title: Developing Pluripotent Stem Cells to Model and Treat Lung Disease
text:
Lung diseases, such as those caused by gene mutations, result in significant morbidity and mortality
worldwide. The advent of stem cell discoveries and regenerative medicine presents new opportunities to
improve our understanding of these diseases and to develop new treatment approaches. Here we propose a
Program Project Grant, composed of 4 integrated projects and 2 cores, whose goal is advancing the latest
discoveries in stem cell biology, human organoid culture models, and gene editing to better understand and
develop new treatments for genetic lung diseases.

title: Methods to Rapidly Explore Combinatorial Diversity and their Application to CRISPR-Cas9 Systems
text:
Here we propose to develop a method for rapidly permuting through combinatorial protein space
at rates two orders of magnitude greater than what is currently available. Using our approach, we
will generate a set of advanced CRISPR-Cas9 transcriptional regulators, and apply these tools to
perform a series of in vivo screens within an animal model of neurodegeneration. The outlined
work will be impactful in several ways as we will establish a new paradigm by which designer
proteins are developed, create a series of highly-potent CRISPR tools with which users can probe
gene function, and provide a general framework for performing precise genetic screens within
complex tissues.

title: The role of microbiota amino acid metabolism in cancer
text:
The microbes living on/in the human body, known as “the human microbiota”, metabolize various dietary
nutrients, train the human immune system, and are essential for human health. This proposal aims to dissect
the molecular mechanisms behind microbiota and cancer association and provides mechanistic insights into
microbiota pathways involved in mediating host amino acid homeostasis and affecting tumor onset and
progression. It will also pave the way for systematically regulating these health-related microbial pathways in the
human gut using synthetic biology and microbial genetics to promote cancer prevention and treatment.

title: Training in Oncology Population Sciences (TOPS)
text:
Research investigation in population science is essential to ensure that discoveries from molecular medicine
and clinical trials translate to routine practice and ultimately decrease the population-level burden of cancer.
The Dana-Farber Harvard Cancer Center’s (DF/HCC) T32 Training in Oncology Population Sciences (TOPS)
program equips postdoctoral fellows with the skills necessary to evaluate cancer care quality and
effectiveness, and to develop, test and implement interventions to improve care delivery thereby ensuring that
T1/T2 discoveries translate across the T3/T4 bridge to achieve maximal impact on population health.
Postdoctoral fellows pursue a two-year program of mentored research, coursework and professional skills
training that supports innovation and leverages the expertise of DF/HCC faculty to prepare them for
independent investigation in cancer-focused population science.

title: Structure-informed dissection of cancer-specific intracellular and paracrine networks
text: Understanding cancer cell-autonomous behavior and recruitment of pro-malignant subpopulations to the tumor microenvironment (TME) is critically dependent on the generation of accurate and comprehensive cellular and intercellular networks. The goal of Project 1 is to develop a novel, integrated, and extensively validated framework to model, manipulate, and dissect cell-cell signaling in the tumor microenvironment involving extracellular ligand-receptor interactions coupled to intracellular signaling networks. Project 1 will build on the methodologies and results generated during the previous CSBC funding period to address multiple challenges by (a) expanding structure-informed prediction of protein-protein interactions (PPI) networks by leveraging novel deep learning approaches, (b) improving signal transduction networks based on the analysis of time-dependent drug perturbation assays, and (c) elucidating ligand/receptor-mediated paracrine interaction networks that mediate recruitment—and possibly reprogramming—of healthy cells to the TME to create a pro-malignant environment. To accomplish these goals, the focus will be on two highly aggressive tumors—colon adenocarcinoma (COAD) and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC)—for which data, models, reagents, and analytical tools were generated during the prior funding cycle. Project 1 is based on three specific aims. Through the integration of deep learning approaches to protein-protein interactions and the creation of structure-based networks for the Hallmarks of Cancer, Aim 1 will provide a 3D-structural context for the proposed work throughout Project 1. Aim 2 will define phosphoproteomics-based intracellular signaling networks and describe their response to drug perturbations. Aim 3 will define paracrine-based cell-cell signaling networks and validate them with a novel organs-on-a-chip platform. The impact of Project 1 will derive largely from its innovative approaches, which include the use of structure-based analyses to model protein interaction networks; the integration of structure-based modeling with deep learning algorithms, including Protein Language Models, to provide models for essentially all interactions that will be predicted and observed in the proposal; the inference of phosphoproteomics-based phosphoprotein activity to provide critical time-dependent and perturbation-sensitive components of cellular signaling; the incorporation of paracrine signaling; and novel experimental validation technologies including matched phosphoproteomic and transcriptional profiles, and the bioengineering of tumors and normal cells within interconnected micro-chambers to better recapitulate tissue physiology in vivo. The major deliverable for Project 1 is an interrogable and holistic model for coupled intra- and inter-cellular signaling which will serve as the foundation for the entire center by enabling the dissection of the mechanisms contributing to the stability of tumor-related cell states, their ligand/receptor-mediated interaction with other subpopulations in the TME, and their pharmacologically actionable molecular dependencies. Project Summary/Abstract

title: High-Performance Next-Generation SPECT-CT (NxSPECT) for Theranostics
text:
This project aims to develop NxSPECT, a next-generation clinical SPECT/CT system featuring stationary, full-
ring, multi-pinhole architecture with a ten-fold sensitivity increase compared to traditional dual-head SPECT/CT
and a six-fold increase compared to the ring-like CZT SPECT/CT. When combined with advanced SPECT image
reconstruction, its high-sensitivity data provide the quantitative accuracy required for dosimetry-guided
personalized radiopharmaceutical therapy (RPT), significantly broadening the scope of SPECT both in clinical
and research settings.

title: Targeting alternative isoform variation for TCR discovery in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer
text:
High-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC) is the most common and aggressive subtype of tubo-ovarian
cancers. This project will comprehensively elucidate the landscape of alternative mRNA processing and the
resulting full-length transcript and protein isoform variation in HGSOC, with the objective of discovering novel
immunotherapeutic targets. Our research seeks to find new targets and therapeutic reagents for adoptive T-cell
therapy and evaluate their efficacy in pre-clinical models of HGSOC.

title: Identifying targetable metabolic vulnerabilities in p53-deficient head and neck cancer
text:
Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is a significant global health challenge, with over 70% of
cases involving inactivation/loss of the tumor suppressor p53. Despite its critical role in preventing tumor
growth, p53 is considered 'undruggable,' and efforts to develop p53-specific therapies have been unsuccessful.
The proposed research will investigate how loss of p53 cellular activity rewires cholesterol metabolism and
inflammation to create targetable vulnerabilities that can be leveraged to kill cancer cells and enhance
immunotherapy responses to improve outcomes for HNSCC patients.

title: Linking signaling to gene expression with mechanistic modeling and machine learning
text:
Immune cell function is controlled by signaling processes that direct the expression of specific sets of response
genes. This project will develop a computational framework that reveals mechanisms by which signaling controls
gene level activity, applying it to understand effects of JAK inhibitors, immunomodulatory drugs that are used to
treat a variety of inflammatory disorders. This work will support the development of more precise treatments for
modulating immune responses in disease.

title: Genome-wide prediction of gene function in Candida auris through transcriptomic and structural analysis
text:
Determining functional information from genomic sequences is critical in characterizing and responding
to the emergence of novel pathogens. This project leverages high-throughput RNA sequencing and protein
structure modeling to predict and experimentally validate protein function in the emerging fungal pathogen
Candida auris. These studies will both provide a framework for other emerging pathogens, while also
producing a co-expression network and describing transcriptional stress responses of C. auris for usage by the
broader fungal pathogenesis field.
